title: How do we match objects with their views?
description: Eight everyday objects, a jug, a funnel, a hammer, a car, a slide, a chair, a ceiling fan and a pressure cooker, are each matched with their front, top and side views by looking for the most telling view of each.
teaching_notes: One idea: each object has one view that gives it away, so look for that view first and then confirm with the other two. Watch for students who match on one view that two objects share.

source: Figure it Out (views of solids, question 3)
video_script.why: The child matches each object with its views by asking what the eye meets from the front, from above and from the side, because one view usually gives the object away.
video_script.substitution: jug: top view a circle with a spout and a handle sticking out; funnel: front and side views funnel shapes, top view a circle with a dot at its centre; hammer: a long handle with the head seen end on from one side; car: a long rectangle from the top and a car profile from the side; slide: a ladder and a ramp in the side view; chair: a seat square from the top and a chair profile from the side; ceiling fan: blades edge on from the front and side, three blades from the top; pressure cooker: a pot with a handle from the front, a circle with a handle from the top.
video_script.anchor: the eight objects in a row, each with three empty frames for the front, top and side views
video_script.payoff_line: Match each object by its most telling view. The jug has a circle with spout and handle. The fan has three blades from the top

final_answer.value: Match each object by its most telling view, such as the circle with spout and handle for the jug and three blades from the top for the fan
final_answer.spoken: match each object by its most telling view, such as the circle with spout and handle for the jug and three blades from the top for the fan

hold_back: Match each object by its most telling view, such as the circle with spout and handle for the jug and three blades from the top for the fan
maths_rules: views are taken as front, top, side
jug: top view a circle with a spout and a handle sticking out
funnel: front and side views funnel shapes; top view a circle with a dot at its centre
hammer: a long handle with the head seen end on from one side
car: top view a long rectangle; side view a car profile
slide: the side view shows a ladder and a ramp
chair: top view a square seat; side view a chair profile
ceiling fan: front and side views show the blades edge on; top view shows three blades
pressure cooker: front view a pot with a handle; top view a circle with a handle
check: the funnel and the pressure cooker both show a circle from above, so one view cannot settle a match; the dot at the centre or the handle on the side tells them apart
video_script.design: One idea: the method of the worked cylinder, repeated for each object. Each object stands on the stage in turn; an eye moves to the front, above and the side, and the most telling view glows in its frame.
